summary: Revision 2 of the Tinkerdeck tidy-up builds on revision 1 and is window-only: no Rust command, permission, CSP, config or data change. Every existing screen, panel, dialog, banner, the footer and the separate editor view stay exactly as they are. R9 is deliberately narrow after the requirements change: the only remembered layout is the sidebar's expanded/collapsed flag already stored in localStorage key td.sidebarCollapsed with a try/catch fallback; revision 2 stores no per-app drawer or console state and restores none. App.tsx never reads a saved git-tools, drawer or console state; openApp closes the git drawer and, through new optional controlled GitBar props, collapses the git tools, and it selects the app's first terminal (or no tab when it has none) so opening an app always starts from the calm default, while a console opened during the session stays mounted and running. The footer gains one toggle that calls the same toggleSidebar handler and reads the same paneCollapsed state as Ctrl+B, so the two cannot disagree, and the footer itself is always rendered (R6). The command palette becomes a cmdk 1.1.1 (MIT) list, still lazy and mounted only while open, inside the existing dialog shell and button rows (Command.Item asChild), with a case-insensitive name filter and the existing 'No commands match.' empty result; it lists every app-level command - global: Toggle sidebar (Ctrl+B), Refresh everything (F5), Switch light/dark theme (Ctrl+Alt+T), Open command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), Open/close editor, Check for updates, Help, Add app, Go to Home, Find themes and Reset layout (No shortcut); app-only: Edit app, Start all, Stop all, Start/Stop/Restart selected terminal, Git fetch/pull/push/sync, Show/Hide git tools, Git: show changes, Git: show history, Close git drawer, Open console, Hide console and New console (No shortcut) - each with its real shortcut from the shared registry or a visible 'No shortcut' note and a visible disabled reason where it cannot run now. Typing a hidden command's name filters to it and running it performs the same action, and commands that exist only while an app is open are listed only then. The editor's own file commands, the Shell and individual theme choices, the branch choice, app and terminal rows, and context-specific dialog answers stay on their visible controls and are not palette commands (R7). R8 is exactly the narrowed requirement: only the git tools (chip collapse), the git drawer (Close) and the console (a new Hide console) get hide paths; Hide console selects a terminal in the same app and leaves its xterm mounted and running, and is shown disabled with a visible reason when the console is the only workspace (an app with no terminals). Each hidden tool reopens from the same control (the git chip, the drawer's Changes/History buttons, the Console tab) and from its palette command. Banners (folder lock, job warning, update, manual-update result, error), dialogs and terminal panes keep the close and dismiss controls they have today; this revision adds none for them and removes none, and Reset layout closes no banner or dialog and discards no unsaved input. Reset layout is a palette command with a 'No shortcut' note that returns the sidebar to expanded, collapses the git tools, closes the git drawer and hides a hideable console, without stopping any terminal (R8). R10 records every building block: cmdk 1.1.1 (MIT, peer React ^18 || ^19, latest, DOM-only so it runs in WebView2 without Tauri APIs or CSP change, headless so the app's CSS variables theme it) for the palette; the shared in-house shortcut registry for shortcuts (it must also drive the non-DOM xterm pass-through, so a hook library cannot replace that half and four shortcuts do not justify a dependency); the existing in-house Dialog shell for dialogs (same title/children/actions, first-action focus, Escape and overlay close; swapping to Radix would change focus behaviour and be a replacement R2 rules out); the existing in-house menus (the published jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu 0.0.35 declares ./dist/index.css in its exports but ships no such file, so it cannot be imported styled, and the existing menus are kept per R2); and the existing CSS show/hide for collapsible parts (no resizing is needed and a pane package would restructure the flex app view). The other jattac house-rule libraries do not perform these functions: zest-tabs and jattac-web-poller are already installed and reused; zest-button, zest-textbox, zest-sidekick-menu, zest-responsive-layout, responsive-table and zest-file-upload are not applicable to a footer toggle, a console Hide button, an existing sidebar, an existing layout, no tables and no uploads, so the native controls and existing CSS remain. Scale and cost: cmdk lives only in the existing on-demand palette/dialog chunk and never the entry chunk; the palette is bounded by fewer than 30 fixed commands, so no paging or virtualization is needed; startup pays one localStorage read and each sidebar toggle one write; the change adds no polling, network, backend, stored data or startup work beyond that one boolean, and hiding a console only changes which tab is selected, so no process, output or memory is discarded.

additions.title: Characterization tests before the palette package swap and the new hide controls
additions.why: The palette, footer, console list and git chip are merged code (USR-004) and this revision changes their internals and controls; freezing what they do today keeps filtering, the empty result, choose-then-run, Escape, the footer's current content and the chip/console behaviour from changing silently.
acceptance: Before cmdk is added or the footer, console and git-tools controls change, tests pin today's palette filtering by name, the 'No commands match.' empty result, choose-runs-once-and-closes, Escape-closes, the footer's current version-only content, the git chip expand/collapse and the console list's select/add/close behaviour.

The full suite passes against the in-house palette and again after the cmdk swap with the same observable results, including each action still being a button with its name, its real shortcut or a 'No shortcut' note, and the empty result.
The new tests fail when the corresponding old behaviour is removed.

additions.title: Reuse the existing sidebar preference instead of a new layout record
additions.why: R9 only needs the window-level sidebar state, and the sidebar's collapsed flag is already saved under td.sidebarCollapsed with a safe fallback, so keeping that key avoids a migration and makes it impossible to restore an app's git drawer or console at startup.
acceptance: No new layout key or per-app layout field is written; the only saved layout value is the existing td.sidebarCollapsed flag.
A missing, unreadable or unexpected value starts the sidebar expanded; the value '1' starts it collapsed.
Opening an app never reads a saved git-tools, git-drawer or console state, and restoring the sidebar never starts or restarts a terminal.
